L2.01.title: sh
L2.01.goal: Read and spell words with the digraph `sh` at the start and end of words.

read.A: Dad and I go to the shop. Dad gets fish for us, and a dish for Mom. "The shop is shut at six," Dad says. I wish for a big ship in the tub! Mom can put cash in a box for the shop. "It is on the shelf," Mom says.
read.B: Sam has a job at the fish shop. He gets cash for his boss, and fish for the shop. "The shop is shut at six," Sam's boss says. Sam and his mom wish for ten fish. "It is on the shelf, not in his bag," Sam says.

L2.02.title: ch, tch
L2.02.goal: Read and spell words with `ch` (start, middle, or end) and `tch` (end of a one-syllable word, right after a short vowel).

read.A: Min and Dad chat on the step. "Where did you go?" Min asks. "I ran to fetch the cat," Dad says. The cat sat in the hutch. Min and Dad catch the cat and shut the hutch. Min and Dad chat and chat. Min is rich in fun, if not in cash!
read.B: Sam and his boss chat at the shop. "Where did you go?" the boss asks. "I had to fetch cash for the shop," Sam says. Sam has a job at ten. Sam's boss is not rich, but the shop is a big shop. Sam and his boss chat, and Sam rushes to catch the bus.

L2.03.title: th (voiced and unvoiced)
L2.03.goal: Read and spell words with `th`, in both its sounds: unvoiced /θ/ (think, bath) and voiced /ð/ (this, then).

read.A: Min and Dad were at the bath. "Where were you?" Mom asks. "I ran from the path to fetch this," Dad says. Min sits in the bath with a thin moth. "Can a moth swim in a bath?" Min asks. "Not this moth," Dad says, "but you can!"
read.B: Sam and his boss were at the shop. "Where were you?" his boss asks. "I ran from the bus stop to fetch this," Sam says. Sam sits and acts fast. "I can fix this fast," Sam says. His boss sits, then says, "I will check on this and fix it fast."

L2.04.title: wh
L2.04.goal: Read and spell words that start with `wh`.
L2.04.newToday: `wh` (usually the plain /w/ sound; a few speakers/dialects say a puff-of-air /hw/ — either is acceptable)

read.A: Min asks Mom, "When will Dad come back?" "Dad will come back at six," Mom says. "Which mug is for some milk?" Min asks. "This mug," Mom says, and fills it with milk. Min sits and grins. When Dad comes back, Min claps and grins.
read.B: Sam asks his boss, "When will the cash come in?" "The cash will come in at six," his boss says. "Which bin is for some of the stock?" Sam asks. "This bin," his boss says, and fills it with stock. Sam sits and grins. When the cash comes in, Sam claps and grins.

L2.05.title: ng, nk
L2.05.goal: Read and spell words ending in `ng` and `nk`.
L2.05.newToday: `ng` /ŋ/, `nk` /ŋk/ (both are single sound-units at the end of a syllable, right after a vowel)

read.A: Min sings a song. "I want a pink hat," Min says. "When the song is done, you can have a pink hat," Dad says. Min sings and sings until the song is done. Dad claps, and hangs a pink hat on Min.
read.B: Sam wants his job done fast. "When is the job done?" his boss asks. "It is done at six," Sam says. Sam picks up his bag and a pink tin king from a bin. "This king is done for," Sam says, and grins. Sam wants to fix it, but the king is just junk.

L2.06.title: Initial blends (st sp sn sm sl sw sk sc bl cl fl gl pl br cr dr fr gr pr tr tw)
L2.06.goal: Read and spell words that start with a two-consonant blend, keeping both consonant sounds distinct (unlike a digraph, both letters keep their own sound).
L2.06.newToday: initial blends `st sp sn sm sl sw sk sc` (s-blends) and `bl cl fl gl pl br cr dr fr gr pr tr tw` (l-blends and r-blends)

read.A: Min and Dad go to the pond. / "Can we swim?" / Min asks. / "Push the flip flops on fast," / Dad says. / A frog sits on a black rock. / Min wants to grab it, / but the frog can hop and skip fast! / "Let's clap and stomp," / Min says, / "then we can swim." / Dad and Min swim, / and Min wants to put the flip flops on the rock.
read.B: Sam must push to get the shop's stock done. / He picks up a black pen / and jots the stock on a pad. / A big box hits the step, / and Sam has to dash and shut it fast. / "I still must push to get this done," / Sam says, / "but a big box will not stop me." / Sam sits, / and gets the job done. / Sam wants to put the pen back on the desk.

L2.07.title: Final blends (-st -nd -nt -mp -sk -lt -ft -lk)
L2.07.goal: Read and spell words that end in a two-consonant blend.

read.A: Dad and Min set up a tent on the sand. / Min helps Dad pull the tent up. / "Pull fast!" / Dad says. / Min pulls and pulls until the tent is up. / Dad packs the milk and a gift in a bag. / Min helps hunt for the best spot to camp. / At dusk, / Min and Dad sit and rest, / full and glad.
read.B: Sam must pull the stock bin to the desk. / "Pull it fast," / his boss says. / Sam pulls and pulls until the bin is at the desk. / Sam checks the list, / packs the gift, / and gets it done. / The shop is full of stock, / and Sam is glad the job is done.

L2.08.title: Three-letter blends (str spr scr spl squ shr thr)
L2.08.goal: Read and spell words that start with a three-consonant blend.
L2.08.newToday: `str spr scr spl squ shr thr`

read.A: "Who has a shrimp and a squid?" / Min asks. / "Min has a shrimp and a squid," / Dad says. / "Could we splash them in the sink?" / Min asks. / "You could splash them in the tub," / Dad says. / Min and Dad splash the shrimp and squid in the tub. / Min grabs a strap and helps scrub the tub. / "This is a thrill!" / Min says, / and grins.
read.B: "Who could help scrub the shop?" / Sam's boss asks. / "I could," / Sam says, / and grabs a strap to fix the bin. / Sam splits the job with a pal. / Sam scrubs the mats, / and checks the straps on the bin. / Sam thinks the shop is strict but fun. / At the end, / Sam is glad the job is done.

L2.09.title: Adding -s and -es (plural and 3rd-person endings)
L2.09.goal: Read and spell words with the `-s` and `-es` endings, and know the rule for which one a word needs.
L2.09.newToday: the `-es` spelling rule (after `s, x, z, ch, sh`, add `-es` instead of plain `-s`, because you cannot say two hissing/buzzing sounds in a row without a vowel between them)

read.A: Min washes the dishes and stacks the boxes. / "Would you help with the mugs?" / Mom asks. / "I would," / Min says, / and picks up the mugs. / "Should I stack them fast?" / Min asks. / "You should stack them fast," / Mom says. / Min washes, / stacks, / and fixes the mugs / until the job is done.
read.B: Sam fixes the vans and checks the boxes. / "Would you help me?" / his boss asks. / "I would," / Sam says, / and picks up the boxes. / "Should we stack them fast?" / Sam asks. / "You should stack them fast," / his boss says. / Sam checks, / stacks, / and fixes the vans / until the job is done.

L2.10.title: Adding -ed (three sounds: /t/ /d/ /ɪd/)
L2.10.goal: Read and spell words with the `-ed` ending, in all three of its sounds.
L2.10.newToday: `-ed` says `/t/` (after an unvoiced sound: jump**ed**), `/d/` (after a voiced sound: grinn**ed**), or `/ɪd/` (after `t` or `d`: want**ed**, end**ed**) — one spelling, three sounds, and none of them is "ed" said as its own syllable except the `/ɪd/` case.

read.A: Min jumped and jogged for fun. / "Did you want your bag?" / Mom asked. / "I packed four mugs in it," / Min said. / Min packed four mugs in a bag, / and rested on the step. / "You packed your bag fast," / Mom said, / and hugged Min. / Min grinned and rested, / glad the job was done.
read.B: Sam checked and fixed the vans. / "Did you want your list checked?" / his boss asked. / "I checked four vans," / Sam said. / Sam packed his bag, / and rested for ten. / "You fixed your job fast," / his boss said, / and grinned. / Sam packed, / jogged off, / and rested, / glad the job was done.

L2.11.title: Adding -ing and -er (no base change)
L2.11.goal: Read and spell words with `-ing` (an action happening now) and `-er` (the person or thing that does it, or "more"), where the base word needs no spelling change at all.
L2.11.newToday: `-ing`, `-er` (added straight onto the end — no doubling, no dropping letters; those spelling rules are their own lesson later, in Level 4)

read.A: Min is packing and stacking many bags. / "Are you helping her?" / Mom asks Dad. / "I am helping her fast," / Dad says. / Min is filling and checking any bag Dad hands her. / "You are a fast helper," / Dad says. / Min is still packing, / glad to help.
read.B: Sam is checking and fixing many vans. / "Are you helping her?" / his boss asks. / "I am helping her fast," / Sam says. / Sam is stacking and packing any bin his boss hands her. / "You are a fast helper," / his boss says. / Sam is still checking, / glad to help.

L2.12.title: Compound words and closed 2-syllable words
L2.12.goal: Read and spell compound words (two whole words stuck together: *sunset*) and closed-syllable 2-syllable words (*rabbit, napkin*) by splitting them into two readable chunks first.
L2.12.newToday: compound words; the VC/CV 2-syllable split (find the vowel in each half, split between the two middle consonants, read each closed syllable on its own, then blend the two chunks together)

read.A: Min packs a backpack / for a picnic. / Does Min pack a napkin? / Min packs a napkin / and a muffin. / Dad packs two bits of catfish. / Min spots a rabbit / and a magnet in the grass. / Dad and Min sit / and watch the sunset. / Min goes to get the picnic bag, / then goes back to sit with Dad. / "Let's have a picnic," / Min says, / and Dad grins.
read.B: Sam packs his backpack / for his shift. / Does Sam pack a magnet? / Sam packs a magnet / for fixing the bus panel. / Sam checks for an insect problem / in the back bin. / Sam fixes a dent with the magnet trick. / This shop had a contest / for the best fix. / Sam goes to get his kit, / then goes back to fix the last dent. / At sunset, / the job is done, / and Sam packs up, / glad and full.

L2.13.title: Review (everything from Level 2)
L2.13.goal: Consolidate every grapheme and ending taught in Level 2 before the mastery check — no new phonics content today, just cumulative retrieval practice at the hardest level the learner has reached.
L2.13.heartLine: again, friend, because (the last 3 of Level 2's 29)

read.A: Min and Dad go to visit a friend. / They pack a backpack with a napkin / and a muffin. / "I want to bring the pink rabbit," / Min says, / "because it is fun." / Min and the friend run and jump in the grass. / When they get to the pond, / they sit still. / A fish splashes, / and Min spots an insect on a twig. / The friend is helping Min hunt for bugs. / "Should we catch it?" / the friend asks. / "No, / let's just watch it," / Min says, / "because it is not bad." / They pack up at sunset, / and hug the friend. / Min and Dad go back, / glad and full, / and plan to come again.
read.B: Sam has a shift with a friend from a shop, / helping fix a big backlog of dents and checks. / "This job is a lot, / but his friend can help," / Sam says, / "because two friends finish fast." / They pack the kit, / check the list, / and split the job up. / Sam's friend fixes the dents, / and Sam checks the vans / and prints the list. / At dusk, / the shop has a full stock of fixed vans / and a strong stack of finished checks. / "We should do this again," / Sam's friend says. / "Yes, / because it went fast and we still got it done," / Sam says, / and they clap hands, / glad and calm.

L2.14.title: Level 2 Mastery Check
L2.14.goal: Confirm the learner has met every Level 2 exit criterion before starting Level 3.
L2.14.newToday: nothing — this is the gate, not a teaching lesson.
